# Chronological account: OpenClaw issue #36142

**Source:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36142 — "Silent empty response when LLM rate limit hits mid-turn (after tool calls)". Filed 2026-03-05 by JaewookYou against OpenClaw 2026.3.3, model `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`, channel Discord. Closed 2026-04-22 as stale by the repo bot. Supplemented by the five fix PRs (#36143, #36169, #36193, #36206, #47046), the prior issue #26905 that the report builds on, a corroborating log analysis posted by a third user on PR #47046, and the current state of `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` on `main`.

## 1. The setup

The reporter ran OpenClaw as a Discord-connected assistant powered by Claude Opus 4.6. The environment had two things going on at once:

- **Five or more concurrent sub-agent sessions**, also on Opus, which the reporter says were consuming the Anthropic API rate-limit quota shared by the account.
- **A main session** in Discord in which the user sent a message that required the model to use tools (the report names `exec`, `read`, etc.).

## 2. What the agent did in the turn

The observable sequence for the failing turn, per the issue's repro steps and the gateway log:

1. The user's message arrives in the main Discord session and an embedded agent run begins.
2. The model emits one or more **tool calls** (exec / read style). OpenClaw executes them.
3. The **tool calls complete successfully.** Their results are rendered into the Discord UI — the reporter states "the user sees tool call results in the UI."
4. The tool results are appended to the transcript and OpenClaw issues the **next LLM request**, whose purpose is to have the model produce its text response given the tool results.
5. **That request fails with an API rate-limit error (HTTP 429 / overload).** The gateway logs:
   ```
   [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: isError=true error=⚠️ API rate limit reached.
   [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="FailoverError: ⚠️ API rate limit reached."
   ```
6. The embedded run **ends**. Its result carries `meta.error` set to the rate-limit error, and its `payloads` array contains no assistant text.
7. The runner's post-run handling inspects the result. At the time, this handling (added for #26905) only checked whether the embedded error was a **context-overflow** error. It was not, so the branch was skipped and the code fell through to `return { kind: "success" }` with empty payloads. The reporter's PR diff shows the pre-fix guard verbatim:
   ```ts
   if (finalEmbeddedError && isContextOverflowError(finalEmbeddedError.message) && !hasPayloadText) {
     return { kind: "final", payload: { text: "⚠️ Context overflow — ..." } };
   }
   return { ... kind: "success" ... }
   ```
8. **Nothing is delivered to Discord.** The assistant turn is empty. The reporter writes: "Completely silent/empty assistant turn… No error is logged to the chat… conversation appears dead."

## 3. Signals available vs. signals surfaced

- **Available internally:** The error was fully known to the system. The embedded runner logged `isError=true` with the exact rate-limit text; the diagnostics lane logged a `FailoverError`. The run's `meta.error` carried the message.
- **Surfaced to the user:** Nothing. The issue notes a contrast: when the same rate-limit error hits **before** any tool call, a separate code path ("Embedded agent failed before reply") does surface a user-facing message. Only the **post-tool-call** position of the error caused the silent result.
- The reporter's expected behavior was an explicit chat message, e.g. "⚠️ API rate limit reached mid-turn — the model couldn't generate a response after tool calls completed. Please try again in a moment."

## 4. Corroborating trajectory from another user (PR #47046 thread, 2026-03-18)

User `infichen` posted a condensed log of the same shape of failure on a different provider (a 429 "qpm超过限流值" from a MiniMax-backed deployment), which adds detail on what the runner did after the error:

```
[line 83]  MODEL RESPONSE  stopReason=error  (1st 429 — inline retry triggered ✅)
[line 84]  embedded_run_agent_end  isError=True  failoverReason=rate_limit
[line 85]  embedded run agent start  (retry, same runId)
...
[line 96]  MODEL RESPONSE  stopReason=error  errorMessage="429 ..."  (2nd 429 — NO retry ❌)
[line 97]  embedded run done  runId=203b445c  aborted=false
[line 98]  lane task done  lane=main
[line 99]  lane task done  lane=session:...
[line 100] setEmoji (cancel)  msgId=<first-user-msg-id>   ← reply context destroyed
[line 101] MODEL REQUEST  (delayed retry fires — outside session lifecycle)
...
[line 107] MODEL RESPONSE  stopReason=stop  ← valid reply, but silently dropped
[line 128] (next user message arrives — no reply was ever sent)
```

Observed there: a first mid-run 429 was retried inline; a second 429 on the *final* model call was not retried inline. The run was marked done with `aborted=false`, session state went idle (`run_completed`), the channel's "typing" emoji was cancelled, and *then* a delayed retry fired outside any live session/lane context. That retry succeeded — the model produced a complete `stopReason: stop` text — but with no reply handle left, the text was discarded. The user saw nothing for the original message.

## 5. Outcome

- **For the user in the turn:** tool side-effects had already executed and their results were visible, but no assistant text and no error was ever posted. The conversation looked stuck until the user sent another message.
- **For the codebase:** Within ~90 minutes of the report, four independent PRs (#36143 by the reporter, #36169, #36193, #36206) proposed essentially the same change — extend the post-run guard to also match rate-limit/overload errors when there is no payload text. A fifth (#47046) followed on 03-15. None of the five were merged; all were closed by the stale-PR bot or by their authors for queue-management reasons. The issue itself was labeled `stale` on 04-17 and auto-closed 04-22.
- **On `main` today**, `agent-runner-execution.ts` contains a block commented "Surface rate limit and overload errors that occur mid-turn (after tool calls) instead of silently returning an empty response. See #36142." It classifies `meta.error` via `classifyFailoverReason`, and if the reason is `rate_limit` or `overloaded` and no non-error content exists, it injects a user-facing error payload (marked `isError: true`) into `runResult.payloads` so it flows through the normal success path rather than early-returning. So the behavior was fixed via a different commit than any of the linked PRs.
- A later related issue (#55451, 2026-03-27) reports the follow-on operator problem: even once errors are surfaced, OpenClaw rewrote the raw provider text into generic copy, hiding the actionable TPM details that were still present in the session transcript.

## 6. Facts worth carrying into the diagnosis step (no classification yet)

- The **model itself never produced a faulty response** in the failing turn; the final model request was rejected by the provider before any tokens were generated. All of the observable "agent behavior" — tool calls, then silence — was determined by how the harness handled the rejected request.
- The failure was position-dependent: identical error, different handling depending on whether it occurred before or after tool execution.
- Tool side-effects (exec/read) had already been committed before the turn was lost, so the user received partial, unexplained output.
- The load that triggered the rate limit was self-inflicted by the same deployment (5+ concurrent Opus sub-agents spawned alongside the main session).
- The system had the error in hand at two logging points but the user-delivery path was the only place it wasn't propagated.

## Bug Description

When the LLM API returns a rate limit (429) or overload error **after tool calls have already completed** in a turn, the assistant response is completely empty/silent. No error message is shown to the user, no indication of what went wrong, and the conversation appears stuck.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run multiple concurrent sub-agents (e.g., 5+ opus sessions) that consume API rate limit quota
2. In the main session, trigger a turn that involves tool calls (exec, read, etc.)
3. Tool calls complete successfully
4. The next LLM call (to generate text response from tool results) hits API rate limit
5. **Result**: Empty assistant response — no text, no error, conversation appears dead

A user-facing error message like:
> ⚠️ API rate limit reached mid-turn — the model couldn't generate a response after tool calls completed. Please try again in a moment.

Completely silent/empty assistant turn. The user sees tool call results in the UI but no assistant text. No error is logged to the chat.

In `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts`, the post-run error handling only checks for context overflow errors (#26905 fix). #35039 turned out to be unrelated (a gateway auth issue) — the PR comment mis-cited it. I have everything needed. Here is the account.

---

# Chronological account: OpenClaw issue #36142

**Source:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36142 — "Silent empty response when LLM rate limit hits mid-turn (after tool calls)". Filed 2026-03-05 by JaewookYou against OpenClaw 2026.3.3, model `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`, channel Discord. Closed 2026-04-22 as stale by the repo bot. Supplemented by the five fix PRs (#36143, #36169, #36193, #36206, #47046), the prior issue #26905 that the report builds on, a corroborating log analysis posted by a third user on PR #47046, and the current state of `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` on `main`.

## 1. The setup

The reporter ran OpenClaw as a Discord-connected assistant powered by Claude Opus 4.6. The environment had two things going on at once:

- **Five or more concurrent sub-agent sessions**, also on Opus, which the reporter says were consuming the Anthropic API rate-limit quota shared by the account.
- **A main session** in Discord in which the user sent a message that required the model to use tools (the report names `exec`, `read`, etc.).

## 2. What the agent did in the turn

The observable sequence for the failing turn, per the issue's repro steps and the gateway log:

1. The user's message arrives in the main Discord session and an embedded agent run begins.
2. The model emits one or more **tool calls** (exec / read style). OpenClaw executes them.
3. The **tool calls complete successfully.** Their results are rendered into the Discord UI — the reporter states "the user sees tool call results in the UI."
4. The tool results are appended to the transcript and OpenClaw issues the **next LLM request**, whose purpose is to have the model produce its text response given the tool results.
5. **That request fails with an API rate-limit error (HTTP 429 / overload).** The gateway logs:
   ```
   [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: isError=true error=⚠️ API rate limit reached.
   [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="FailoverError: ⚠️ API rate limit reached."
   ```
6. The embedded run **ends**. Its result carries `meta.error` set to the rate-limit error, and its `payloads` array contains no assistant text.
7. The runner's post-run handling inspects the result. At the time, this handling (added for #26905) only checked whether the embedded error was a **context-overflow** error. It was not, so the branch was skipped and the code fell through to `return { kind: "success" }` with empty payloads. The reporter's PR diff shows the pre-fix guard verbatim:
   ```ts
   if (finalEmbeddedError && isContextOverflowError(finalEmbeddedError.message) && !hasPayloadText) {
     return { kind: "final", payload: { text: "⚠️ Context overflow — ..." } };
   }
   return { ... kind: "success" ... }
   ```
8. **Nothing is delivered to Discord.** The assistant turn is empty. The reporter writes: "Completely silent/empty assistant turn… No error is logged to the chat… conversation appears dead."

## 3. Signals available vs. signals surfaced

- **Available internally:** The error was fully known to the system. The embedded runner logged `isError=true` with the exact rate-limit text; the diagnostics lane logged a `FailoverError`. The run's `meta.error` carried the message.
- **Surfaced to the user:** Nothing. The issue notes a contrast: when the same rate-limit error hits **before** any tool call, a separate code path ("Embedded agent failed before reply") does surface a user-facing message. Only the **post-tool-call** position of the error caused the silent result.
- The reporter's expected behavior was an explicit chat message, e.g. "⚠️ API rate limit reached mid-turn — the model couldn't generate a response after tool calls completed. Please try again in a moment."

## 4. Corroborating trajectory from another user (PR #47046 thread, 2026-03-18)

User `infichen` posted a condensed l

{"evidence": "In the failing turn the Opus 4.6 model issued tool calls that executed successfully, then OpenClaw sent the follow-up LLM request to generate the text reply; the Anthropic API rejected that request with a 429 rate-limit/overload error (quota consumed by 5+ concurrent Opus sub-agent sessions). Gateway logs show `embedded run agent end: isError=true error=⚠️ API rate limit reached.` and `FailoverError: ⚠️ API rate limit reached.`; no tokens were generated. OpenClaw's post-run guard only mapped context-overflow errors to user-facing text, so the run returned `kind: \"success\"` with empty payloads and the user saw tool results followed by silence.", "reasoning": "The first fault in the chain is the upstream LLM host abruptly terminating the final request with a rate-limit error before any model output existed — the model never reasoned, acted, or produced a faulty response, so no model-fault subtype (Recovery Failure, Tool Recovery Failure, Satisficing) applies; the model had no turn in which to recover. The silent empty reply is a downstream symptom of the harness lacking a mapping for this error at the post-tool-call position, which is exactly the 'unmapped rate limit' case named under Service Failure. Mistranslation (model — tool) is the closest alternative, but that concerns garbling data across the model↔environment boundary, whereas here the environment→model request itself was killed and the delivery gap is harness→user, not a mis-marshaled observation or action. Orchestrator Delegation Failure was considered because concurrent sub-agents exhausted quota, but the source attributes that load to the operator's setup rather than a model decision, so it is not the agent's fault.", "category": "env (external) — model", "subtype": "Service Failure"}
